target_customer: B2B sales and marketing teams that buy custom lead and contact data
problem: Sales teams needed accurate, custom lead and account data that databases could not supply; the company combined a managed human workforce with machine learning to build it.

founders.name: Anand Kulkarni
education: UC Berkeley (MobileWorks began as a grad school project, per a secondary source)
founders.background_notes: Described as co-founder of MobileWorks in a 2011 era paper summary; education detail rests on a secondary source.

founders.name: Prayag Narula
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; co-author of the 2011 MobileWorks HCOMP poster.

competitors.name: Amazon Mechanical Turk
competitors.what: Anonymous crowd marketplace for micro tasks

competitors.name: CrowdFlower
competitors.what: Data management tasks for large firms routed to Mechanical Turk and other crowds

technical_complexity.rationale: Managed crowd workflow, quality control and machine learning on top, a standard but operations heavy build.

defensibility.rationale: Lead data and managed workforce could be copied; incumbents like ZoomInfo and DiscoverOrg held large databases.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The original crowdsourcing wedge was not absorbed; the company moved into lead data and stayed independent.

market_need_then: Mobile crowd work for people in India and Pakistan was a 2011 pilot with 99 percent accuracy in a 10 user study, and demand for lead data grew later.

identity.voice_and_tone: Opinionated industry commentary on the company blog

rebrands.why: Not stated; a secondary source says it was known as MobileWorks until at least 2015 and the LeadGenius mark was registered in 2015

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name with limited press about the brand; the company blog is active but no community or virality evidence was found.

pivots.from: MobileWorks crowdsourcing platform for low cost mobile workers
pivots.to: LeadGenius account based lead generation data
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; the lead data product launched by the 2014 Series A

outcome_analysis: The company began as MobileWorks, a mobile crowdsourcing platform, and pivoted into account based lead generation data. It raised about $20M across Series A and B plus smaller rounds, bought WhoKnows software assets in July 2023, and reports 150+ customers. It remains active with no exit; its own 2023 article says it had gone three years without layoffs, a self reported claim.
notes: Series A and B are from the press release and Demand Gen Report as read in search summaries; the pages themselves were not opened (one returned 403). The Series B lead differs by aggregator (Lumia vs Sierra). The December 2016 $4M round and May 2018 $3M round rest on single outlets or an aggregator and stage labels are unstated, so they use other. Aggregator totals range $16M to $22M. Competitor list is as of the MobileWorks 2011 product, not lead data. Founder education and employers not found in opened sources.
